title: Factors Associated With the Autonomy of Patients Treated by Haemodialysis in Community Centres. A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study. PARTICIPANTS: All patients receiving haemodialysis in community centres in a French region on December 31, 2021. MEASUREMENTS: Patient characteristics and multiple dimensions of patient autonomy were recorded. Multivariate analyses assessed associations between patient factors and technical autonomy. RESULTS: Among 507 patients, 304 were treated in self-care units and 203 in satellite haemodialysis units. Patients in satellite haemodialysis units had a median age of 69 years (IQR 59-78; range 24-90), compared with 66 years (IQR 54-75; range 22-91) in self-care haemodialysis units. They also had more comorbidities. Younger age was associated with greater autonomy in arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), setting the haemodialysis machine (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), and programming it (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Autonomy differed significantly between centres, with centre affiliation significantly associated (p < .001) with autonomy for the arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing and machine-related tasks. CONCLUSIONS: Patient characteristics in self-care haemodialysis units did not fully explain autonomy for haemodialysis tasks. Considerable variability between centres was observed, suggesting that centre-related factors may contribute to differences in patient autonomy.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units.

title: The complexity of provoked venous thromboembolism: one treatment plan does not fit all.
abstract: The decision of whether to continue patients diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE) on anticoagulation after the initial treatment period is often nuanced. Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE. In addition, major transient risk factors generally carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE than minor transient risk factors. However, many patients will also have ≥1 persistent VTE risk factor, which further increase the risk for recurrence. Some persistent risk factors, such as inflammatory bowel disease, are associated with a sufficiently high risk of recurrent VTE, for which guidelines recommend indefinite anticoagulation. There are multiple other persistent risk factors that carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE, such as chronic renal insufficiency and obesity. The HI-PRO (High-Risk Patients with Provoked Venous Thromboembolism) trial sought to assess the efficacy and safety of extended thromboprophylaxis for the prevention of recurrent VTE in patients with an initial provoked VTE and at least 1 persistent risk factor. The study found a lower risk of recurrent VTE in the thromboprophylaxis cohort, challenging the traditional time-limited treatment for provoked VTE, but heterogeneity of the study population and small sample size preclude identification of which subsets of patients could safely discontinue anticoagulation. We consider the conundrum of provoked VTE in this review.

Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE.

title: A Versatile, Patient-Centred Approach to Surgical Wound Closure: A Single-Centre Case Series on the Use of a Synthetic Electrospun Fibre Matrix in Vasculopathic Patients.
abstract: Patients with vascular disease often suffer from lower extremity ulcerations that may require surgical intervention to remove non-viable or infected tissues. Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications. A synthetic electrospun fibre matrix (SEFM) (Restrata, Acera Surgical Inc.) is a fully synthetic, extracellular matrix that encourages cellular infiltration and neovascularization with minimal inflammatory response. In the present study, a single vascular surgeon retrospectively reviewed data of vasculopathic patients treated with SEFM during surgical management of various wound aetiologies. Ten patients were identified and data on time to closure, closure approach and post-operative complications were collected and analysed. SEFM was utilized to either support neo-vascularization for subsequent autografting or re-epithelialization through secondary intention healing. All patients in this series achieved either definitive closure or complete re-epithelialization in an average of 6.8 weeks. One instance of superficial infection was successfully managed with antibiotics. No instances of unplanned re-operation or other wound complications were observed. Early experience suggests practical application of SEFM for surgical wound management in vasculopathic patients.

Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications.

title: Effectiveness of Tomazoni Measurement Method for Central Catheter Tip Positioning in Neonates: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) tip positioning in neonates remains challenging, with high rates of malposition reported using traditional measurement methods. AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method. STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025. RESULTS: Of 62 randomised procedures, 55 were evaluable (27 in the experimental group, 28 in the control group). Central positioning was achieved in 21 of 27 procedures (77.8%) in the experimental group versus 5 of 28 (17.9%) in the control group (p < 0.001). PICC insertion procedures assessed using the Tomazoni method were 4.36 times more likely to achieve central tip placement (RR = 4.36; 95% CI: 1.91-9.88). Catheter withdrawal was required in 3 of 27 procedures (11.1%) in the experimental group versus 16 of 28 (57.1%) in the control group (p = 0.001; RR = 0.19; 95% CI: 0.06-0.59). CONCLUSIONS: The Tomazoni measurement method was associated with substantially higher rates of central PICC tip positioning and reduced need for catheter withdrawal compared with the traditional method. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The Tomazoni method offers a reproducible, low-cost measurement strategy that can be implemented in neonatal intensive care units to improve catheter positioning accuracy and reduce procedure-related manipulations, with potential implications for patient safety. The trial, titled 'Comparison between measurements of peripherally inserted central catheters in children and newborns', was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier RBR-55zwb45. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method. STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025.

title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement. STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool. RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps. CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
abstract: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.

title: [Abdominal aortic aneurysms: diagnosis, risk stratification and treatment strategies].
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is defined as a focal aortic dilation ≥3.0 cm in maximum diameter, with rupture-associated mortality approaching 80%. Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women. Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) provides an early survival benefit, with 30-day mortality of 1.8% vs 4.3% for open repair in the EVAR-1 trial, and substantially comparable long-term outcomes up to 15 years of follow-up, at the cost of a 15-20% reintervention burden and the need for lifelong imaging surveillance. Accordingly, the 2024 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider EVAR as the preferred treatment in most patients with favorable anatomy, reserving open repair for young patients with long life expectancy, unfavorable anatomy and specific conditions such as connective tissue disease, inflammatory aneurysms, graft infection and failed previous endovascular repair. Treatment selection should be based on the integrated assessment of individual operative risk, aortic anatomy and life expectancy.

Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized.

title: Biological sex differences in the United States CTEPH Registry.
abstract: RATIONALE: Biological sex underpins phenotypic differences in many cardiopulmonary conditions. In pulmonary hypertension, most studies have focused on the "sex paradox" in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where females are more susceptible to PAH but have better right ventricular function, better response to PAH medications, and better survival than males. Sex differences have also been observed in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) but are less well characterized. OBJECTIVES: To investigate sex differences in males and females diagnosed with CTEPH in the United States. METHODS: Using the multicenter United States CTEPH Registry, we explored sex differences in a CTEPH population at baseline and follow-up. We collected data every 6 months for a total of 48 months. Sex was determined from self-reported "male," "female," or "transgender" categories recorded on case report forms. We report descriptive analyses comparing male and female characteristics. We examined prespecified variables of interest using regression modeling, including adjustment for age, body mass index (BMI), and interaction terms (sex vs age, sex vs BMI). Survival analysis was performed with Cox proportional hazards modeling. RESULTS: Females (n = 367, 49.1%) had greater BMI than males (median [IQR] F: 32 kg/m2 [26.6, 38.8] vs M: 28.7 kg/m2 [25.5, 33.8]). Males were more likely to have a recognized history of acute deep vein thrombosis (OR 2.6; CI 1.9-3.5). Males had better baseline PH-specific health-related quality of life (HRQoL) by EmPHasis10 (-3.3; CI -5.0- (-1.7), World Health Organization functional class (FC III/IV OR 0.52, CI 0.37-0.74) and longer 6-minute walk distance (+82.3 m, CI 56.4-108.2). Males were less likely to have distally located disease (OR 0.53, CI 0.35-0.78) and were less likely to have inoperable CTEPH (OR 0.62, CI 0.40-0.96). Post-PTE, females had persistently worse HRQoL and function, with increased need for adjunctive therapies. There was no difference in overall survival between males and females (HR 1.11; CI 0.71-1.75). CONCLUSIONS: Males and females may have distinct CTEPH phenotypes, which impact access to and feasibility of PTE. There are sex-associated disparities in the experience of CTEPH as a disease state, and differential impacts on HRQoL that warrant further investigation.

In pulmonary hypertension, most studies have focused on the "sex paradox" in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where females are more susceptible to PAH but have better right ventricular function, better response to PAH medications, and better survival than males. Sex differences have also been observed in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) but are less well characterized.

title: Underdetected peripheral artery disease in people with hypertension: A narrative review of risk-stratified case-finding, diagnostic pathways, and equity in care.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common but often underrecognized in people with hypertension because symptoms are frequently absent or atypical and access to physiologic testing is uneven. This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening. METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources. Evidence was interpreted according to the question it could answer: association/prognosis, diagnostic accuracy, treatment effect, implementation, or policy status. RESULTS: Hypertension and PAD share age-related, metabolic, renal, and tobacco-related determinants, while pressure-related vascular injury provides biological plausibility for their association. Resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the initial physiologic test for appropriately selected people; toe-brachial index with waveforms is preferred for noncompressible ankle arteries, exercise ABI for persistent exertional symptoms despite normal or borderline resting values, and duplex ultrasound when anatomic definition will change management. Guideline-supported risk-based testing differs from universal screening of unselected asymptomatic adults, for which outcome benefit remains unproven. Detection is clinically meaningful only when linked to appropriate prevention, symptom management, foot protection, and referral. CONCLUSION: This narrative review supports a risk-stratified, treatment-linked approach to PAD recognition in hypertension care, but the proposed case-finding pathway itself has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes. Pragmatic trials of the complete care pathway are needed.

This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening. title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown. METHODS: Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR. RESULTS: p p p p p p 3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, < 0.01; high: $39,431, = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804). CONCLUSIONS: In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.

The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown. METHODS: Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified.

title: In-Hospital Outcomes and Mortality After Revascularization for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia by Maintenance Dialysis Status: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2006-2020.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited. METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression. RESULTS: Of 7,962 eligible hospitalizations, 411 (5.2% of the unweighted sample) involved maintenance dialysis. Maintenance dialysis was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.96), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.46), prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.41), transfusion (aOR 1.43), sepsis (aOR 1.88), pneumonia (aOR 1.69), multiorgan failure or shock (aOR 1.80), and venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.06). Hospital charges were also higher (adjusted beta USD 17,497), whereas urinary tract infection odds were lower (aOR 0.68). DISCUSSION: Maintenance dialysis was associated with greater in-hospital morbidity and mortality among CMI-coded revascularization hospitalizations. The inability to distinguish stable from acute-on-chronic CMI limits interpretation as an elective cohort. Findings support individualized perioperative assessment without establishing causation or optimal treatment timing.

METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression.

title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The safety of intravenous thrombolytics for ischemic stroke in pregnancy is largely unknown. We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy. METHODS: We used the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines to conduct the review. We searched 3 databases (OVID Medline, EMBASE, Scopus) for studies published up to October 2025. We analyzed outcomes in a Bayesian aggregated case series to compare rates of adverse outcomes in our cohort with those in the general population. Elective termination and spontaneous abortion were grouped together, given that it was often difficult to determine whether complications of thrombolysis may have played a role in the decision for termination. RESULTS: We included 123 studies of 216 patients (median age 31 years) treated with thrombolytics during pregnancy, of whom 85 had ischemic stroke. Six of the 32 total fetal deaths were deemed likely to be causally related to thrombolytics (3 in stroke). The risk of miscarriage in our thrombolysis population was 12.4% higher (95% credible interval [CrI]: 2.6%, 23.2%) than published general pregnant population rates, and the risk of stillbirth was 5.9% higher (95% CrI: 1.6%, 12.7%). The proportion of pregnant patients with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage was similar between our pregnant cohort and young, nonpregnant patients receiving thrombolytics (risk difference -0.4%; 95% CrI: -0.8%, 2.7%). DISCUSSION: Thrombolytics were likely causally associated with a small minority of published cases of fetal death after thrombolysis in pregnancy. There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: The study protocol was pre-registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024605043).

We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy.

title: Anticoagulation stewardship quality improvement project to decrease incidence of supratherapeutic activated partial thromboplastic time in overweight cancer patients on unfractionated heparin infusions.
abstract: 2 2 2 2 Unfractionated Heparin (UFH) is widely used to treat multiple conditions in hospitalized patients. Standard dosing based on actual body weight (ABW) may lead to over-anticoagulation in overweight patients due to the limited vascularity of adipose tissue. Historically, ABW was used when BMI ≤ 40 kg/m, and adjusted body weight (AdjBW) when BMI > 40 kg/m. However, patients with ABW >130% of ideal body weight (IBW) and BMI ≤ 40 kg/mexperienced increased rates of supratherapeutic activated partial thromboplastin times (aPTTs). The objective of this project was to evaluate whether use of AdjBW for initial UFH dosing reduces supratherapeutic aPTTs in cancer patients with ABW >130% of IBW and BMI ≤ 40 kg/m. A new high intensity UFH protocol utilizing AdjBW UFH dosing was implemented on July 9, 2024. This single-center quality improvement study compared the pre- and post-intervention aPTTs in hospitalized cancer patients. In the bolus/transition cohort the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs decreased by 37% (RR 0.63; 95% CI: [0.46-0.86], p = 0.004 and the percentage of first therapeutic aPTTs increased by 82.1% (RR 1.82; 95% CI: [1.12-2.97], p = 0.03. In the no bolus cohort, the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs decreased by 39.2% (RR 0.61; 95% CI 0.38-0.97, p = 0.04). Time to therapeutic aPTT was shorter in the post-implementation arm compared to pre-implementation. In conclusion, AdjBW-based UFH dosing significantly reduced the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs and decreased the time to first therapeutic aPTT in obese cancer patients on the high-intensity UFH protocol.

title: One-hour pulsatility index as an independent predictor of futile recanalization after successful mechanical thrombectomy: A prospective observational study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Futile recanalization (FR) - poor functional outcome despite successful mechanical thrombectomy - affects approximately 40% of patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion. Reliable bedside predictors of FR at the time of recanalization remain lacking. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled 122 consecutive patients with successful thrombectomy (mTICI ≥2b; all mTICI 2b cases corresponded to eTICI 2b67) between 1 October 2025 and 12 April 2026. Pre-procedural optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) was measured by ultrasound, and post-procedural transcranial color-coded Doppler measurements were obtained by an investigator who was not involved in the endovascular procedure and was blinded to the thrombectomy technique and angiographic reperfusion findings. FR was defined as 90-day mRS 3-6. Discriminative performance was assessed by ROC analysis with DeLong comparison; independent predictors by multivariable logistic regression with bootstrap validation (5000 resamples). RESULTS: FR occurred in 48 patients (39.3%). The 1-hour symptomatic-hemisphere pulsatility index (PI) was markedly elevated in FR patients (1.23 vs. 0.81; p < 0.001; AUC 0.922, 95% CI 0.861-0.984). At a threshold > 0.99, sensitivity was 91.7% (95% CI: 80.4-96.7%) and specificity 89.2% (95% CI: 80.1-94.4%).Preoperative ONSD was also higher in FR patients (5.2 vs. 4.7 mm; p < 0.001; AUC 0.785). The combined model reached AUC 0.934, without significant incremental gain over PI alone (p = 0.062). On multivariable analysis, 1-hour PI (OR 2.929; p < 0.001) and admission NIHSS (OR 1.457; p = 0.009) were independent predictors. Predictive accuracy was preserved in the local anesthesia subgroup (AUC 0.895). CONCLUSIONS: The 1-hour symptomatic PI was independently associated with futile recanalization and showed high discriminatory performance after thrombectomy. Preoperative ONSD may provide complementary risk stratification. Multicenter external validation is warranted.

Reliable bedside predictors of FR at the time of recanalization remain lacking. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled 122 consecutive patients with successful thrombectomy (mTICI ≥2b; all mTICI 2b cases corresponded to eTICI 2b67) between 1 October 2025 and 12 April 2026.

title: Controversies and reappraisal in the management of distal deep vein thrombosis: From evidence-based discrepancies to risk-stratified individualized strategies.
abstract: BackgroundDistal deep vein thrombosis (DVT) confined to the infrapopliteal deep venous system, commonly termed isolated distal deep vein thrombosis (IDDVT), accounts for a substantial proportion of lower-extremity DVT. Its optimal management remains controversial because randomized evidence is limited, patient populations are heterogeneous, and guideline recommendations differ.ObjectiveThis narrative review critically examines the evidence for anticoagulation and serial ultrasonographic surveillance in IDDVT, evaluates sources of uncertainty, compares major guideline recommendations, and proposes a cautious, risk-adapted framework for individualized management.MethodsWe searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library to identify English-language guidelines, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and relevant observational studies addressing IDDVT management, thrombus extension, pulmonary embolism, bleeding, post-thrombotic syndrome, and treatment duration. The search was updated through July 2026. Priority was given to major guidelines, randomized trials, and contemporary systematic reviews/meta-analyses, with older studies retained when providing foundational evidence.ResultsCurrent evidence does not support a uniform treatment strategy for IDDVT. The choice between anticoagulation and serial imaging should consider symptom severity, extension risk factors, bleeding risk, thrombus location, patient preferences, and feasibility of follow-up imaging. Randomized trials support surveillance in selected patients and suggest reduced recurrent VTE with extended anticoagulation in patients who tolerate initial treatment. However, evidence remains limited by small or selected populations, heterogeneous outcomes, and extrapolation from proximal DVT or pulmonary embolism.ConclusionIDDVT should be managed according to individual risk rather than as a homogeneous condition. Decisions regarding anticoagulation initiation and treatment duration should be considered separately. Serial imaging is reasonable for selected patients without severe symptoms or major extension risk factors, whereas anticoagulation is generally favored in those with severe symptoms or recognized extension risk factors. No IDDVT-specific risk score has been validated, and interventional treatment should remain exceptional because direct evidence is lacking.

title: Utilizing evidence-based diagnosis and treatment for central venous thrombosis: closing the gaps where guidelines fail.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Catheter-related thrombosis (CRT) is a frequent complication of central venous catheters and accounts for most upper extremity deep vein thrombosis events. Despite its increasing clinical burden, management remains poorly standardized because recommendations are largely extrapolated from general venous thromboembolism studies rather than CRT-specific evidence. AREAS COVERED: We performed a structured comparative review of major international, European, and North American guidelines, consensus documents, and position statements identified through PubMed, Ovid, and Scopus searches covering January 2016 to March 2026. Nineteen documents from vascular medicine, oncology, and vascular access societies were included. Recommendations on diagnostic strategies, imaging modalities, catheter management, anticoagulant selection, treatment duration, and invasive interventions were systematically compared. EXPERT OPINION: Considerable heterogeneity persists across recommendations. Ultrasound is consistently endorsed as the first-line imaging modality, whereas the role of clinical prediction scores and D-dimer remains uncertain because neither has been validated in CRT populations. Catheters should be preserved when functional, correctly positioned, and free from infection. Anticoagulation for at least three months is universally recommended, while invasive procedures should be reserved for selected patients with extensive thrombosis or life- or limb-threatening complications. Prospective studies are urgently needed to validate diagnostic algorithms, optimize anticoagulant strategies, and develop CRT-specific evidence-based pathways.

title: Effect of Endostaple Configuration and Oversizing on Endograft Displacement Force: An In Vitro Evaluation of the Aortoseal Endostapling System.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Proximal endograft fixation remains a key determinant of long-term durability of endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). The Aortoseal Endostapling system consists of a nitinol frame with 6 welded endostaples at the proximal end, intended to enhance fixation and seal of an endograft by mimicking the hand-sewn anastomosis of open aortic repair. This study evaluates the effect of different distributions of activated endostaples on endograft displacement force (EDF), while considering various endograft oversizing options. METHODS: An in vitro silicone tube model was used to assess EDF at 2 mm endograft displacement and pull-out force across 11 activated staple configurations of the Aortoseal Endostapling system with 10%, 20%, and 30% endograft oversizing. Interobserver agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), based on a 2-way mixed-effects model for absolute agreement. RESULTS: Intraclass correlation coefficient for interobserver agreement was 0.987. Endograft displacement force ranged from 8.8 N ± 0.15 N to 39.6 N ± 2.96 N across all configurations and oversizing conditions. Incorporation of the Aortoseal frame alone, without staple activation, substantially increased EDF compared with no Aortoseal frame at 10% and 20% oversizing. Furthermore, EDF was mostly influenced by the number of activated staples and the maximum unstapled circumferential angle (MUCA). The 6-activated-staple configuration consistently yielded the highest EDF. The effect of oversizing on EDF was inconsistent across configurations at 10% and 20%, whereas 30% oversizing was associated with lower EDF in most configurations. Pull-out force exceeded EDF in all tested configurations except the 1-activated-staple configuration. CONCLUSION: In this in vitro study, Aortoseal frame incorporation alone substantially increased EDF relative to the graft-only configuration at 10% and 20% oversizing. Ten percent endograft oversizing yielded EDF values comparable with 20% oversizing across most configurations. Circumferential staple distribution was the primary determinant of EDF in the Aortoseal Endostapling system, with EDF decreasing with increasing MUCA and increasing with staple number across all endograft oversizing conditions, consistent with circumferential load sharing as a potential underlying mechanism. These findings may serve as a mechanistic reference framework for preoperative planning in anatomically challenging cases and warrant further experimental and clinical evaluation.Clinical ImpactThe Aortoseal Endostapling system (Endoron Medical Holdings Ltd., Dublin, Ireland) represents a novel approach to proximal endograft fixation, enabling simultaneous circumferential single-stage activation of 6 nitinol endostaples via balloon activation, providing a uniform and reproducible fixation pattern intended to mimic the longitudinal and radial anchoring of a surgical anastomosis. To support clinical implementation, this study systematically evaluated endograft displacement force across a range of activated staple configurations, including suboptimal deployment scenarios. The findings provide physicians with a mechanistic reference framework for preoperative planning, supporting procedural decision-making in anatomically challenging cases.

This study evaluates the effect of different distributions of activated endostaples on endograft displacement force (EDF), while considering various endograft oversizing options.

title: Five-Year Prognostic Outcomes After Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Treatment According to Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia Status: Insights From the BIOLUX P-III Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of death, limb loss, and impaired functional recovery despite revascularisation. Drug-coated balloons may reduce restenosis and repeat intervention after infrainguinal endovascular therapy, but long-term safety and effectiveness data in patients with CLTI remain limited. METHODS: We performed a prespecified subgroup analysis of BIOLUX P-III, a prospective international post-market all-comers registry evaluating the Passeo-18 Lux paclitaxel-coated balloon for infrainguinal peripheral artery disease. Outcomes were compared between patients with and without CLTI through 60 months. Endpoints included freedom from major adverse events, clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation, major target-limb amputation, amputation-free survival and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event outcomes were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods. Because follow-up completeness declined substantially by 60 months, late estimates were interpreted in the context of censoring, attrition and competing mortality. RESULTS: P P P P P Among 877 treated patients, 328 (37.4%) had CLTI. Technical success exceeded 98% in both groups. Patients with CLTI had greater baseline comorbidity, more advanced limb threat and more frequent below-the-knee disease. At 60 months, freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation was 85.3% in patients with CLTI and 78.3% in those without CLTI ( = .59), and freedom from major adverse events was similar (76.5% vs 74.3%; = .13). In contrast, 5-year survival was substantially lower in patients with CLTI (47.9% vs 76.7%; < .001). Freedom from major target-limb amputation was lower (93.3% vs 99.3%; < .001), and amputation-free survival was reduced (47.1% vs 75.7%; < .001). Patients with CLTI received a lower cumulative paclitaxel dose despite higher mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Passeo-18 Lux treatment was associated with preserved lesion-level durability through 5 years, but CLTI identified a high-risk prognostic phenotype with poor survival and limb outcomes. These findings suggest that long-term outcomes in CLTI are influenced by systemic comorbidity, early limb vulnerability, competing mortality and wound-related factors beyond lesion-level device performance alone.Clinical ImpactThis study provides clinically relevant insights into the long-term outcomes of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) undergoing endovascular revascularisation with drug-coated balloons. Despite high procedural success, patients with CLTI experience substantially greater long-term mortality and adverse limb outcomes than those with intermittent claudication. These findings highlight the importance of recognising CLTI as a high-risk clinical phenotype requiring comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction, multidisciplinary management, and structured postprocedural surveillance. The study's principal contribution is its evaluation of five-year outcomes in a real-world, all-comers population, providing valuable evidence to inform patient counselling, individualised treatment strategies, and long-term clinical decision-making.

Drug-coated balloons may reduce restenosis and repeat intervention after infrainguinal endovascular therapy, but long-term safety and effectiveness data in patients with CLTI remain limited. METHODS: We performed a prespecified subgroup analysis of BIOLUX P-III, a prospective international post-market all-comers registry evaluating the Passeo-18 Lux paclitaxel-coated balloon for infrainguinal peripheral artery disease.

title: Differential Effect of Endovascular Treatment in Medium or Distal Vessel Occlusion: A Distal Secondary Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion stroke are heterogeneous. Randomized trials show no net benefit of endovascular treatment (EVT) over best medical treatment (BMT) alone, which may mask heterogeneity of treatment effect. We used an externally developed machine learning model to predict excellent early neurological outcome (EENO) with BMT alone and examined whether the effect of EVT differed across predicted risk. METHODS: A Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) model was trained to predict EENO (24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score of 0-2) in patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion treated with BMT alone in a local Bernese Stroke Registry. This model was applied to patients from the DISTAL randomized trial (55 centers and 11 countries), who were randomized to EVT plus BMT or BMT alone. We tested for interaction between predicted EENO and treatment allocation on the primary outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale shift), repeating this using admission NIHSS alone. RESULTS: P P interaction interaction In the development cohort (n=257, 42% female, and mean age 70.4±14.8 years), 54% achieved EENO. In the DISTAL cohort (270 BMT alone, 269 EVT plus BMT, 44% female, and mean age 74.9±12.0 years), the model showed moderate external discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.73). A significant interaction was found between predicted EENO and treatment effect (=0.012): in 152 patients predicted to achieve EENO, EVT was associated with worse 90-day modified Rankin Scale score (common odds ratio, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.27-0.84]), whereas no treatment effect was seen in 387 patients predicted not to achieve EENO (common odds ratio 1.13 [95% CI, 0.79-1.60]). A model using admission NIHSS alone showed comparable discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.71) and a common odds ratio for EVT of 0.47 (95% CI, 0.25-0.89) in patients with an NIHSS score of ≤4 and a common odds ratio of 1.05 (95% CI, 0.75-1.47) in patients with an NIHSS score of >4 (=0.029). CONCLUSIONS: EVT was harmful in patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion predicted to achieve EENO with BMT alone, and an NIHSS-alone model performed comparably to the multivariable model. title: Preoperative Imaging-Derived Factors Associated With Spinal Cord Ischemia After Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair-A Scoping Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Spinal cord ischemia (SCI) after fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/B-EVAR) is a devastating complication with a non-negligible incidence, and better risk prediction is necessary. Preoperative imaging allows assessment of anatomical and morphological characteristics that may predispose to SCI. This scoping review aimed to systematically search the literature and provide an overview of the current evidence on the association of preoperative imaging-derived factors with SCI after F/B-EVAR. METHODS: This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. A systematic literature search of PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, and Web of Science was performed from database inception to October 21, 2025, to identify studies that reported on the association of preoperative imaging-derived factors with SCI following F/B-EVAR. Only studies published in English were included. Studies were screened by 2 reviewers, and data were charted using a standardized data-extracting form. Identified factors were categorized as aortic-related, aortic side-branch-related, thrombus-related, and miscellaneous factors. RESULTS: A total of 2231 studies were identified, and 45 were included in this scoping review. Included studies consisted of observational cohort studies and nonrandomized investigational device exemption studies, with all studies using univariable and multivariable analyses. A total of 18 imaging-derived factors were identified and categorized into aortic-related (33 studies), aortic side-branch-related (17 studies), thrombus-related (5 studies), and miscellaneous (psoas muscle parameters, median arcuate ligament [MAL]) (6 studies). Aneurysm extent, maximum aortic diameter, and rupture were the most frequently reported investigated factors. Most (n = 39, 87%) studies were performed in cohorts of less than 400 patients. Definitions of similar investigated factors varied, and associations found were variable across studies. Only a limited number of included studies performed a multivariable analysis. CONCLUSION: This scoping review provides a categorized overview of preoperative imaging-derived factors and their associations with SCI after F/B-EVAR. Identified factors showed heterogeneous associations and inconsistent definitions across studies limited comparability. Large prospective cohort studies, including standardized definitions of parameters, are needed to investigate the influence of preoperative imaging-derived factors on the risk of SCI.Clinical ImpactSpinal cord ischemia (SCI) after fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair remains a significant complication despite continual advancements in preventive strategies and identification of clinical risk factors. Preoperative imaging allows assessment of anatomical and morphological characteristics that may predispose to SCI. This scoping review provides a categorized overview of preoperative imaging-derived factors and the evidence on their association with SCI. Identified factors had varying definitions and showed heterogeneous associations with SCI. Recommendations for future research are outlined to further optimize SCI risk prediction using preoperative imaging-derived factors.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Spinal cord ischemia (SCI) after fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/B-EVAR) is a devastating complication with a non-negligible incidence, and better risk prediction is necessary. Preoperative imaging allows assessment of anatomical and morphological characteristics that may predispose to SCI. This scoping review aimed to systematically search the literature and provide an overview of the current evidence on the association of preoperative imaging-derived factors with SCI after F/B-EVAR.

title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Determinants of Bowel Ischemia and Associated Risk After Elective Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Bowel ischemia (BI) is an uncommon but devastating complication of elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify patient- and procedure-related risk factors for BI after elective EVAR. METHODS: I 2 We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, Cochrane Library, Scielo, and Lilacs from database inception through March 31, 2024, without language or date restrictions. We included observational studies of adults who underwent elective EVAR and reported postoperative BI and extractable risk-factor data. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, extracted data, and assessed study quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. For factors reported in multiple sufficiently homogeneous studies, random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences (MDs), with heterogeneity assessed using. RESULTS: I I I I I 2 2 2 2 2 Twenty-three retrospective cohort studies, including 306 344 elective EVAR procedures, met the inclusion criteria, and 10 provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis. Across all studies, 1535 patients developed postoperative BI, corresponding to an overall incidence of approximately 0.5%. Female sex was associated with increased BI risk (RR, 2.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.06-3.43; = 0%). Larger aneurysm diameter was also associated with increased risk (MD, 4.05 mm; 95% CI, 0.09-8.02; = 0%). Renal dysfunction was a consistent predictor, with chronic kidney disease (RR, 2.93; 95% CI, 1.01-8.47; = 29%) and dialysis dependence (RR, 5.35; 95% CI, 2.38-12.05; = 0%) associated with BI. Major intraoperative blood loss >1 L conferred the highest relative risk among pooled factors (RR, 7.45; 95% CI, 2.80-19.85; = 0%). Age, systemic arterial hypertension, and active smoking were not significantly associated with BI in pooled analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Bowel ischemia after elective EVAR is uncommon but clinically important because delayed recognition carries substantial morbidity and mortality. Female sex, larger aneurysm diameter, chronic kidney disease, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss identify patients who may warrant heightened perioperative vigilance. The certainty of evidence remains very low, and future studies should standardize reporting of bowel segment, mesenteric vessel involvement, inferior mesenteric artery and internal iliac artery status, endograft configuration, and overlapping registry populations.Clinical RelevanceBowel ischemia after elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare, but its low incidence should not be interpreted as low clinical importance because delayed diagnosis is often catastrophic. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes the largest available elective EVAR evidence focused on bowel ischemia and identifies reproducible risk signals, including female sex, aneurysm size, renal dysfunction, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss. The practical gain for readers is not a definitive prediction score, but a clearer framework for perioperative judgment: recognize vulnerable patients, avoid overinterpreting weak or non-poolable associations, and apply heightened postoperative vigilance when embolic, hypoperfusion, pelvic collateral, or renal-risk features coexist.

title: Delayed and prolonged hypotension and watershed cerebral infarction following coil embolization of an extracranial carotid artery aneurysm: A possible baroreceptor-mediated complication.
abstract: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare vascular lesions increasingly treated by endovascular approaches when open repair is unfavorable. Although hemodynamic depression related to carotid baroreceptor activation is recognized during carotid interventions, delayed and prolonged hypotension after primary coil embolization of an ECAA is rarely reported. A 64-year-old man underwent primary coil embolization for an enlarging high cervical ECAA because severe proximal internal carotid artery tortuosity precluded safe stent reconstruction. After an initially uneventful recovery, progressive hypotension developed approximately 1-2 hours after the procedure and ultimately required vasopressor support through postoperative day 16. Recurrent hypotension was followed by acute neurological deterioration. Computed tomography angiography showed no large-vessel occlusion, aneurysm rupture, or overt parent artery compromise, whereas diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a left watershed infarction consistent with hypoperfusion. Blood pressure augmentation resulted in rapid neurological recovery. Because the aneurysm was adjacent to the carotid bulb, carotid baroreceptor activation related to post-embolization geometric change was considered a possible mechanism. This case highlights the need for careful hemodynamic monitoring after coil embolization of ECAAs near the carotid bulb, even without balloon angioplasty or stent deployment.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance reveals stable myocardial tissue characteristics despite cardiac remodelling after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in liver cirrhosis.
abstract: AIMS: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal hypertension in liver cirrhosis but acutely increases cardiac preload. The present study aimed to prospectively assess changes in cardiac function, remodelling, and myocardial tissue characteristics after TIPS using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). METHODS AND RESULTS: Of the 45 screened patients with advanced liver cirrhosis, 23 patients [median (IQR) age 65 (56-69) years, 70% male, 87% Child-Pugh class B, MELD score 14 (12-20)] were prospectively included and underwent multiparametric CMR before TIPS implantation (CMR-1), as well as follow-up imaging after 3 (2-4) days (CMR-2, n = 20) and 100 (87-122) days (CMR-3, n = 10). Biventricular end-diastolic volumes increased significantly from baseline to the final follow-up (CMR-3) [left ventricle (LV) +27.2 (20.8-38.6) mL/m2; right ventricle (RV) +26.1 (18.2-38.0) mL/m2; both P < 0.001], accompanied by increased stroke volumes [LV +7.2 (3.6-15.7) mL/m2, RV +9.8 (2.3-15.4) mL/m2; both P < 0.001]. LV mass increased from 32 (30-37) g/m2 to 47 (45-52) g/m2 (P < 0.001). Although extracellular volume (ECV) fraction remained unchanged [27 (23-28) % vs. 25 (23-29) %; P = 0.06], ECV mass increased from 17.1 (14.0-21.8) g to 25.4 (20.7-27.4) g (P < 0.001), reflecting the concomitant increase in LV mass. Myocardial tissue characterization revealed no significant changes in native T1 or T2 values during follow-up (all P > 0.05). CONCLUSION: TIPS implantation induces progressive biventricular dilatation, increased stroke volume, and eccentric remodelling. Despite these marked structural adaptations, myocardial tissue characteristics remained largely unchanged during short- and mid-term follow-up, suggesting predominantly preload-driven cardiac remodelling.

title: Haemodialysis in haemophilia B: a case report. Challenges and strategies from a nephrology perspective.
abstract: Haemophilia B, the result of factor IX deficiency, is a complex clinical condition that is particularly challenging when associated with kidney failure. This is primarily due to the high bleeding risk associated with kidney replacement therapies. The increase in life expectancy in haemophilia patients has resulted in a greater prevalence of age-related comorbidities, including chronic kidney disease. Nevertheless, a consensus has yet to be reached regarding the most suitable dialysis modality for this population. In this report, we present a case study of a 68-year-old male patient suffering from severe haemophilia B, who was administered prophylactic Idelvion® (albutrepenonacog alfa) and subsequently underwent arteriovenous fistula creation and haemodialysis initiation without encountering any bleeding complications. This narrative review, from the perspective of a nephrologist, addresses the epidemiology and main clinical considerations regarding dialysis in haemophilia B. These considerations include the choice between haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, vascular access planning, haemostasis management with factor IX replacement, and anticoagulation strategies aimed at minimising bleeding risk. A review of the extant literature and clinical reports published between 2020 and 2025 was conducted, integrating documented experiences and available guideline recommendations. In addition, we put forward a series of pragmatic recommendations that are -underpinned by a systematic decision-making framework. Through meticulous multidisciplinary planning incorporating the utilisation of factor IX concentrates, meticulous surgical techniques, and tailored anticoagulation protocols, patients with haemophilia B can be deemed eligible for chronic haemodialysis with a reasonable degree of safety.

title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. DISCUSSION: + Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

title: High-intensity focused ultrasound as a bridging vascular-modulating therapy for fertility-sparing management of placental site trophoblastic tumor complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) is a rare gestational trophoblastic neoplasm characterized by local invasiveness and marked vascularity. Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases. CASE PRESENTATION: A 23-year-old woman presented with persistently plateaued serum human chorionic gonadotropin levels following hysteroscopic management for suspected incomplete abortion. Imaging revealed a deeply invasive hypervascular uterine lesion with UAVF, raising strong suspicion of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Given her strong desire for fertility preservation and high surgical risk, ultrasound-guided HIFU was performed as an initial vascular-modulating intervention. Subsequent expert pathological review confirmed PSTT. RESULTS: HIFU achieved significant reduction in lesion perfusion and vascular flow, as confirmed by Doppler ultrasound and contrast-enhanced MRI. Although complete tumor ablation was not achieved due to lesion size and deep invasion, subsequent low-dose chemotherapy resulted in complete biochemical remission accompanied by radiologic regression of residual lesions. No major HIFU-related complications were observed, and normal menstrual function resumed during follow-up. CONCLUSION: HIFU is a technically feasible and safe fertility-preserving adjunct for vascular modulation in hypervascular PSTT complicated by UAVF. While HIFU alone may not achieve definitive oncologic control in large or deeply invasive lesions, it can serve as a bridging strategy to reduce tumor perfusion and vascularity, facilitating subsequent systemic therapy in carefully selected patients. This approach demonstrates the potential role of HIFU as a bridging vascular-modulating strategy within multimodal fertility-preserving management.

Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases.

title: Pregnancy and iron deficiency anemia are associated with COVID-19 severity: a retrospective cohort study from Gaza.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 poses significant risks to pregnant women, with pregnancy recognized as a risk factor for severe disease. This vulnerability may be exacerbated by iron deficiency anemia (IDA) due to impaired immune function, reduced oxygen transport, and altered coagulation and endothelial function. METHODS: n n A retrospective cohort study of 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 with COVID-19 was conducted at Al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza (2021). Pregnant ( = 97) and nonpregnant ( = 174) groups were stratified by IDA, investigating the impact of pregnancy and IDA on the severity of COVID-19. Iron deficiency was determined by transferrin saturation levels <20% measured during acute infection, whereas ferritin levels were not available. RESULTS: p p p p p p p p Overall pregnancy was significantly associated with COVID-19 severity ( < 0.001), with pregnant women having higher odds of critical illness (OR = 4.61, 95% CI 2.27-9.39, < 0.001) and death (OR = 5.25, 95% CI 1.91-14.44, = 0.001) compared with moderate illness. All deaths were due to acute respiratory distress syndrome; no venous thromboembolism cases occurred. IDA was associated with COVID-19 severity in both pregnant ( = 0.015) and non-pregnant ( = 0.002) women. In a multivariable model including pregnancy, IDA was associated with higher odds of severe (OR = 3.57, 95% CI 1.97-6.48, < 0.001), critical (OR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.09-4.64, = 0.029), and fatal illness (OR = 7.23, 95% CI 1.96-26.74, = 0.003) compared with moderate illness. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that among young, otherwise healthy, unvaccinated women with COVID-19, pregnancy and IDA are associated with increased COVID-19 severity. However, interpretation requires caution considering the small number of events, particularly deaths, and the assessment of iron status during acute infection using transferrin saturation alone without ferritin measurements, which limits the ability to distinguish preexisting iron deficiency from inflammation-related changes in iron metabolism.

title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis. METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors. RESULTS: p p p p Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, = .039). CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

title: Nurse-led, multidisciplinary strategies to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infections: Parenteral nutrition stewardship and central venous access device maintenance.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs) remain a major source of preventable patient harm and are associated with increased mortality, longer hospital stays, and higher health care costs. Reducing central venous access device (CVAD) utilization and improving line maintenance practices are key strategies for prevention. PURPOSE: To reduce CLABSIs through a nurse-led, multidisciplinary initiative focused on parenteral nutrition (PN) stewardship, CVAD maintenance, and shared accountability for line necessity and care. METHODS: Using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, an interprofessional team implemented a PN clinical decision tree, standardized PN administration kit, targeted nursing education, daily multidisciplinary line rounds, and real-time escalation processes. Outcomes included CLABSI Standardized Infection Ratio (SIR), Standardized Utilization Ratio (SUR), PN-related CLABSIs, and adherence to line care practices. RESULTS: The initiative was associated with a 46% reduction in CLABSI SIR (1.165-0.632), an 11.7% reduction in CVAD utilization (SUR 0.479-0.423; P < .001), and a decrease in PN-related CLABSIs from 45% to 12.5% of all CLABSI cases. Process-related issues identified during rounds decreased from 32.73% to 26.11%. CONCLUSIONS: A nurse-led, multidisciplinary approach combining PN stewardship, standardized CVAD care, and real-time feedback improved patient safety and reduced CLABSI risk. The model offers a sustainable, replicable strategy for infection prevention.

title: Acute-on-Chronic Upper Limb Ischemia Precipitated by Critical Right Brachiocephalic Stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Brachiocephalic artery stenosis is an uncommon cause of upper extremity ischemia and cerebrovascular insufficiency. Diagnosis may be delayed because of subtle clinical manifestations, particularly in patients with established atherosclerotic risk factors. CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old woman with diabetes, dyslipidemia, and active tobacco use presented with progressive bluish discoloration and pain of the right-hand digits. The primary care physician initially misattributed the presentation to Buerger disease. Angiography revealed critical ostial brachiocephalic artery stenosis, and prompt endovascular stenting showed improvement in digital perfusion and eventual resolution of symptoms. DISCUSSION: This case highlights the potential for isolated upper extremity digital ischemia to represent proximal great vessel disease, especially among high-risk smokers. Careful examination and imaging are important for avoiding a missed diagnosis. Smoking cessation remains essential for long-term protection. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Detailed examination and interarm blood pressure measurement should be routinely performed in patients with unexplained upper-extremity ischemia to identify potential proximal great-vessel disease.

Diagnosis may be delayed because of subtle clinical manifestations, particularly in patients with established atherosclerotic risk factors. CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old woman with diabetes, dyslipidemia, and active tobacco use presented with progressive bluish discoloration and pain of the right-hand digits.

title: In Situ Fenestration-Assisted TEVAR in Patients With Complex Pathology Involving the Aortic Arch.
abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the feasibility, safety, and short-term clinical outcomes of in situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair (ISF-TEVAR) employing an electrocautery-connected guidewire combined with a novel, pump-less, extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass for cerebral perfusion in patients with complex aortic arch pathology. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center study included 19 consecutive patients treated between February 2024 and September 2025. A homemade extracorporeal arterio-arterial bypass was constructed using femoral arterial inflow and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) tubing connected to supra-aortic sheaths to maintain continuous cerebral perfusion during fenestration. Fenestrations were performed with an electrocautery-connected 0.018-inch chronic total occlusion-dedicated guidewire. Patients' demographics, procedural details, perioperative outcomes, and early follow-up data were analyzed, with stratification according to the number of fenestrated supra-aortic branches. RESULTS: P A total of 37 supra-aortic branches were targeted: 3-branch fenestrations in 6 patients (31.6%), 2-branch in 6 patients (31.6%), and single-branch in 7 patients (36.8%). Technical success, defined as successful graft fenestration with patent branches on completion angiography, was achieved in 94.5% (35/37). One failed innominate artery fenestration was managed with chimney-assisted TEVAR, and 1 left subclavian artery fenestration was successfully completed in a subsequent procedure. Operative time increased with procedural complexity (140 ± 12 minutes for 1 branch, 152 ± 10 minutes for 2 branches, and 162 ± 13 minutes for 3 branches; = .004). No intraprocedural mortality occurred. Two perioperative strokes (10.5%) and 2 in-hospital deaths (10.5%) were recorded, 1 death was due to vertebrobasilar stroke and the other due to retrograde type A aortic dissection with rupture. Median hospital stay was 8 days. During a mean follow-up of 9.2 months, there was no aorta-related mortality, with an overall survival rate of 89.5%. All stented branches remained patent, and 2 endoleaks (10.5%) were successfully treated endovascularly. CONCLUSION: In situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair using an electrocautery-connected wire combined with a temporary, pressure gradient-driven extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass is a feasible, reproducible, and safe technique for complex aortic arch repair. This fully percutaneous approach ensures continuous cerebral perfusion, demonstrates efficient procedural metrics, and yields favorable short-term outcomes, representing a practical alternative when custom-made devices or hybrid surgical procedures are not available.Clinical ImpactIn situ fenestration-assisted TEVAR combined with a temporary pumpless extracorporeal femoral-carotid bypass enables continuous cerebral perfusion during complex aortic arch interventions without the need for cardiopulmonary bypass or surgical debranching. This technique expands the feasibility of fully endovascular multibranch arch repair in urgent or anatomically challenging cases where custom-made devices are unavailable. For clinicians, this approach offers a practical and reproducible strategy to mitigate cerebral ischemic risk while maintaining procedural efficiency and percutaneous access. This technique may facilitate broader adoption of in situ fenestration by providing a cerebral protection strategy using readily available endovascular equipment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center study included 19 consecutive patients treated between February 2024 and September 2025. A homemade extracorporeal arterio-arterial bypass was constructed using femoral arterial inflow and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) tubing connected to supra-aortic sheaths to maintain continuous cerebral perfusion during fenestration.
