title: Screening for occult cancer in patients with unprovoked VTE: Evolving evidence and emerging risk prediction tools.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) can represent the first clinical manifestation of an underlying occult malignancy, particularly when unprovoked. Large cohort studies and meta-analyses have reported that the risk of cancer is markedly increased in the first 6-12 months following unprovoked VTE, with a 3- to 4-fold higher risk compared with provoked VTE events, particularly among older patients. Certain clinical presentations, including upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), bilateral DVT, splanchnic vein thrombosis, and cerebral venous thrombosis, are associated with a higher prevalence of occult cancer and warrant targeted investigations. Four randomised controlled trials and subsequent meta-analyses comparing limited versus extensive screening strategies (including whole-body CT scan and PET/CT scan) consistently demonstrated earlier cancer detection without a corresponding reduction in cancer-related or all-cause mortality, while extensive screening carries additional costs, radiation exposure, and risks of false-positive findings. Several clinical risk-prediction scores (RIETE, SOME, VTE-Malignancy, CAVE, and machine learning-based models) have been developed to identify patients at higher risk of occult cancer who might derive greater benefit from extensive screening. None of these scores demonstrates sufficiently robust discriminative performance for routine clinical use. Based on the available evidence, we propose a pragmatic, individualised algorithm favouring limited screening for most patients with unprovoked VTE, reserving extensive screening for those with high-risk clinical features following shared decision-making. Ongoing trials and emerging risk-stratification tools may help refine future screening strategies, balancing the benefit of early cancer detection against the risks and costs of extensive investigation.

title: A Branch-Specific Combined Fenestration Strategy for Chronic Aortic Dissection With Severe Paravisceral True Lumen Compression.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate a branch-specific combined fenestration strategy to address the technical challenges of severe true lumen (TL) compression during physician-modified fenestration (PMF)-based four-vessel visceral reconstruction in chronic aortic dissection (CAD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled twenty-three consecutive patients with aneurysmal CAD and severe paravisceral TL compression (minimum functional TL diameter ≤10 mm) treated between January 2020 and December 2024. All patients underwent visceral reconstruction using anterior-branch PMF and bilateral renal in situ laser fenestration (ISLF) performed following TL expansion. Endpoints included technical success (complete four-vessel reconstruction), 30-day mortality, target-vessel patency, and TL expansion. RESULTS: Complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction was achieved in all 23 patients (92/92 target vessels). Renal ISLF was successful in all 46 renal arteries, with first-attempt success in 44 (96%). Distal aortic exclusion was required in 20 patients; one interval infrarenal rupture in the staged group was managed with emergency repair. Over a median follow-up of 17.0 months, primary target-vessel patency was 99% (91/92). The median minimum functional TL diameter increased from 8.0 mm preoperatively to 15.9 mm at one-year follow-up. No type I or III endoleak was identified. Thirty-day mortality was 0%. Transient spinal cord ischaemia occurred in one patient (4%), and acute kidney injury (KDIGO Stage 1) in two patients (9%), all resolving before discharge. CONCLUSION: In highly selected CAD patients with severe TL compression, this combined fenestration strategy enabled complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction with satisfactory early target-vessel patency and no target-vessel loss, though longer follow-up in larger cohorts is required.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Decrease the Rate of Rupture, Cardiac Events, and Death in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a degenerative condition involving several processes including inflammation, matrix remodeling, disruptions of vascular smooth muscle cells, and thrombus formation all leading to progressive dilatation of the aorta and eventual rupture. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. Data is limited on the impact of GLP-1RA on outcomes of patients with AAA. The aim of this study is to examine the association and possible impact of GLP-1RA on patients with AAA. METHODS: Data was sourced from the TriNetX research network, encompassing 123 health care organizations. Utilizing ICD-10 and CPT codes, we identified patients with AAA who received abdominal imaging every six months. Group 1 was comprised of patients who were treated with GLP-1RA while Group 2 patients were not. Propensity-score-matching (PSM) was used in a 1:1 fashion using age, sex, diabetes, metformin use, hypertension, cardiac disease, tobacco use, chronic kidney disease, and pulmonary disease as covariates. Primary outcomes were aneurysm rupture or repair. Secondary outcomes include mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure). Standard statistical methods were used as appropriate. RESULTS: We identified 412,490 patients with diagnosis of AAA who were undergoing 6-month surveillance between June 1, 2010 and April 16, 2024. After PSM, the GLP-1RA group (N=13,722) underwent fewer elective repairs at each timepoint (1.5% vs 2.3% at 2 years, 2.1% vs 3.0% at 5 years, P<.01) and had significantly fewer ruptures at two years (1.1% vs 1.8%, P<.01) and five years (1.6% vs 2.4%, P<.01) when compared to Group 2 (N=13,722). Group 1 also experienced significantly fewer MACE and all-cause mortality at two and five years. On multivariate analysis, GLP-1RA significantly reduced the risk of undergoing elective repair (HR 0.757, 95% CI [0.636-0.902], P<.01), rupture (HR 0.538, 95% CI [0.418-0.691], P<.01), all-cause mortality (HR 0.474, 95% CI [0.439-0.511], P<.001), and MACE (HR 0.825, 95% CI [0.794-0.857], P<.01) at 5 years. CONCLUSIONS: The use of GLP-1RA in patients with AAA is associated with fewer ruptures, elective repairs, and improved rates of MACE and death. A prospective analysis may further elucidate if GLP-1RA should be prescribed to reduce the rate of aneurysm growth.

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. title: The prevalence and long-term clinical significance of left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery in an asymptomatic population.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prevalence of left common iliac vein (LCIV) compression between the right common iliac artery and L5 vertebra in an asymptomatic cohort, and determine whether individuals with ≥50% LCIV stenosis develop chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) or deep venous thrombosis (DVT). DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study with prospective long-term clinical follow-up METHODS: Iliac venous anatomy was analysed on protocolised computed tomography (CT) in healthy individuals assessed for live related kidney donation at a tertiary referral centre between January 2012 and January 2019, with follow-up until January 2026. Scripted phone interviews assessed left leg venous symptoms, signs, investigations and treatment. RESULTS: Of 102 participants, 60 were female (58.8%), median age was 38 years (IQR 30-45), mean body mass index was 26.6 ± 4.2. Mean LCIV compression was 39.2% ± 18.5. Female sex (OR 3.52, CI 1.36-10.1, p=0.009) and younger age (OR 0.91, CI 0.86-0.96, p<0.001) were independently associated with ≥50% LCIV compression. 39 participants (38.2%) had ≥50% LCIV compression; one participant (1%) had ≥70% LCIV compression. One participant developed a right leg DVT. No others underwent venous imaging for CVI or DVT over a median 11-year follow-up (IQR 9.1-12.7). Of 13 participants with ≥50% LCIV compression surveyed, three reported left leg varicosities and three reported an episode of isolated leg swelling without investigation or treatment. CONCLUSIONS: LCIV compression is common on supine CT in healthy, asymptomatic individuals, particularly young females. On long term follow-up, no clinically significant left leg venous sequelae were identified in those with ≥50% LCIV compression. Hence, caution is advised when reporting this finding on CT to avoid unnecessary investigation or intervention.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Thrombin Injection for Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Pseudoaneurysms: Predictors of Failure and Recurrence.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided thrombin injection (UGTI) is effective for iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms, but factors associated with early failure and recurrence remain incompletely defined. We evaluated treatment outcomes and their predictors. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients treated with UGTI between November 2023 and May 2026. Technical success was defined as immediate complete thrombosis after the first injection, clinical success as complete thrombosis at 24-hour Doppler follow-up, and recurrence as recanalization at 24 hours after technical success. Independent associations with clinical failure and recurrence were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 204 patients (94.4%), clinical success in 176 (81.5%), and recurrence occurred in 31 of 204 patients (15.2%). Overall success without surgical or endovascular repair was 94.0%. Therapeutic index procedures (OR, 6.368; 95% CI, 2.037-19.910), INR >1.5 (OR, 5.286; 95% CI, 1.681-16.625), shorter neck length (OR per mm, 0.879; 95% CI, 0.802-0.964), a longer procedure-to-UGTI interval (OR per day, 1.041; 95% CI, 1.008-1.074), and platelet count <150,000/μL (OR, 3.407; 95% CI, 1.174-9.884) were independently associated with clinical failure. Therapeutic procedures (OR, 7.670; 95% CI, 2.094-28.090) and INR >1.5 (OR, 3.653; 95% CI, 1.114-11.982) independently predicted recurrence. No procedure-related complications occurred. CONCLUSIONS: UGTI was highly effective for iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms, with high immediate and overall success and no observed complications. Procedural, anatomical, temporal, and hemostatic factors were associated with outcomes, while clinical failure and recurrence represented distinct treatment phases. These findings may support risk-adapted surveillance.

We evaluated treatment outcomes and their predictors. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients treated with UGTI between November 2023 and May 2026.

title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage.

title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen. SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve.

title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified.

title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

title: Probable Loeys-Dietz Syndrome with aortic root dilatation and multiple arterial tortuosity in resource-limited setting : A case report.
abstract: Loeys-Dietz Syndrome (LDS) is a rare hereditary connective tissue disorder that is characterized by multisystem disorders predisposing individuals to arterial and aortic aneurysms. We present the case of a 17-year-old Bangladeshi male referred to cardiology for assessment of systemic abnormalities and cardiovascular risk. He presented with craniofacial, musculoskeletal, and cutaneous abnormalities including hypertelorism, mandibular ectopic hair, joint hypermobility with mild thoracic scoliosis, residual talipes equinovarus. He had past medical history of surgically corrected congenital anomalies. Based on clinical and radiological findings, he was diagnosed with clinically suspected Loeys-Dietz Syndrome as genetic testing was unavailable. He was managed through a multidisciplinary approach with regular follow-up. This report adds to literature on Loeys-Dietz Syndrome, emphasizing on aortic root dilatation and carotid artery tortuosity as important clinical and radiological features supporting diagnosis of LDS particularly in young patients presenting with characteristic craniofacial abnormalities or suggestive radiological findings. Early recognition and multidisciplinary management are crucial in resource-limited settings to prevent life-threatening vascular complications.

title: Cervical Spine Oncology: Perioperative Management and Complications.
abstract: STUDY DESIGN: Narrative review. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize contemporary evidence on perioperative complications in primary and metastatic cervical spine tumor surgery and to provide an evidence-informed framework for their prevention and management. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Cervical spine tumor surgery converges dense neurovascular and aerodigestive anatomy with a medically fragile, frequently irradiated patient population. Although cervical metastases represent only about 8-20% of spinal metastatic disease, their mismanagement carries disproportionately severe consequences, ranging from disabling pain to high-level paralysis and death. Cervical-specific risk-stratification tools are lacking, and most available evidence is extrapolated from degenerative anterior cervical cohorts. METHODS: This is a narrative review of perioperative complications in cervical spine oncology. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles published through May 2026, prioritizing literature from the past 5 years while including seminal earlier references where foundational, using combinations of the terms "cervical spine," "spinal metastasis," "spinal tumor," "perioperative complications," "airway," "vertebral artery," "wound," "dysphagia," "venous thromboembolism," and "hardware failure." Reference lists of included articles were hand-searched for additional sources. Studies were selected by author consensus for relevance to the complication domains discussed; formal risk-of-bias assessment and quantitative pooling were not performed, consistent with a narrative design. Because oncology-specific evidence is limited, data derived from degenerative cervical cohorts are identified as such throughout. RESULTS: Major complication domains include airway compromise (highest with multilevel corpectomy, combined approaches, and cervicothoracic constructs), vascular and neurologic injury, CSF leak, wound failure and infection in irradiated fields, hardware failure, venous thromboembolism, and dysphagia. CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes depend on preoperative risk stratification, multidisciplinary coordination, and individualized postoperative care rather than any single intraoperative maneuver. Because the evidence base remains largely Level III-IV without validated cervical oncology-specific tools, described practices should be regarded as reasonable, evidence-informed considerations rather than standards of care.

title: Age-dependent impact of diabetes on limb events and mortality in patients with peripheral artery disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with substantial risks of limb events and mortality. Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear. METHODS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, adults with PAD were identified from Clalit Health Services, Israel (2000-2026). Patients were stratified by diabetes status and age at PAD diagnosis (35-50 vs > 50 years). The primary outcome was major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as lower-extremity revascularization or major amputation. All-cause mortality was a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, interaction analyses, and propensity score overlap weighting were performed. RESULTS: P P P P Among 4538 patients aged 35-50 years at PAD diagnosis, 1902 (42%) had diabetes. During a median follow-up of 12.0 years, diabetes was independently associated with higher risks of MALE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-2.01,= .032) and mortality (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.18-1.70,< .001). Diabetes was associated with increased MALE risk in both age groups, with no significant interaction by age (for interaction = .498). In contrast, the association between diabetes and mortality was significantly stronger in patients aged 35-50 years than in those aged >50 years (adjusted HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.72-2.33 vs 1.30, 95% CI 1.27-1.33,for interaction < .001). Excess mortality associated with diabetes emerged during longer-term follow-up. CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with increased risks of MALE and mortality in PAD, with a stronger association with mortality among patients diagnosed before age 50. These findings identify diabetes as a marker of particularly high risk in premature PAD.

Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear. title: Stent-graft placement for an axillosubclavian artery injury in a pediatric patient: A case report.
abstract: Axillosubclavian artery injury is a rare traumatic vascular injury associated with a high mortality rate. Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. Although endovascular stent-graft placement has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open surgery, its application in pediatric trauma patients remains poorly documented. In this report, we present the case of a pediatric patient with traumatic axillosubclavian artery injury successfully treated with stent-graft placement. A 13-year-old boy was transported to a referring hospital following a traffic accident and transferred to our emergency and critical care center. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography conducted on hospital day 2 revealed a pseudoaneurysm due to right axillosubclavian artery injury, prompting endovascular stent-graft placement. The patient was discharged on hospital day 23. Although contrast-enhanced computed tomography at 1-year after discharge confirmed severe stenosis within the stent graft, distal perfusion was maintained. Notably, no ischemic symptoms or growth disturbances were observed in the right upper limb at the 3-year follow-up. Endovascular stent-graft placement appears to be a viable treatment for axillosubclavian artery injury in selected pediatric patients, particularly adolescents.

Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: 2 2 PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using Iand τ. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

title: Ultralow-contrast stepping digital subtraction angiography for whole-limb arterial evaluation: A case report.
abstract: Stepping digital subtraction angiography (DSA) enables whole-limb arterial assessment with a single contrast injection, and diluted contrast medium may further reduce iodine exposure. A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach. Severe right external iliac artery stenosis prompted stepping DSA before and after embolization to evaluate distal embolization. Sevenfold- and tenfold-diluted stepping DSA examinations were performed before and after embolization, respectively, using identical injection parameters (3 mL/s; 30 mL). These required 4.29 and 3.0 mL of undiluted contrast medium, respectively. Although pedal artery enhancement was reduced with tenfold dilution, image quality remained acceptable, and no obvious distal embolization was identified in the visualized arteries; however, small emboli in poorly opacified pedal branches could not be excluded with tenfold dilution. Because internal iliac artery embolization was not expected to significantly alter lower-extremity arterial perfusion, the observed difference in image quality was considered to primarily reflect the difference between the two dilution protocols rather than changes in arterial hemodynamics. Ultralow-contrast stepping DSA may be a contrast-saving technique in selected cases when repeated whole-limb arterial evaluation is required.

A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach.

title: A Novel Hybrid Endovascular Technique for Tympanojugular Paraganglioma: Flow Diversion Followed by Direct Transauricular Squid Embolization.
abstract: Skull-base paragangliomas with persistent internal carotid artery (ICA) supply can be challenging to devascularize safely. We report a 17-yearold male with an Succinate Dehydrogenase Complex Iron Sulfur Subunit B (SDHB)-associated tympanojugular paraganglioma treated using a staged hybrid endovascular strategy after subtotal resection. Persistent supply from a short ICA feeder and circumferential involvement of the petrous ICA precluded safe conventional transarterial embolization. A Surpass Elite flow-diverting stent was deployed across the feeder after dual antiplatelet therapy to preserve parent-vessel patency, reduce tumour inflow, and reinforce the arterial wall. Four months later, protected direct transauricular and transcervical puncture embolization with Squid 12 was performed under intermittent ICA balloon occlusion. Marked tumor devascularization was achieved without embolic or thromboembolic complication, and definitive resection was completed without new neurological or cranial nerve deficit. This staged approach may provide a useful adjunct for selected skull-base paragangliomas with persistent ICA supply when conventional embolization carries unacceptable risk.

title: Association of Estimated Arterial Stiffness with Collateral Status and Functional Outcome after Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the OPTIMAL-BP Trial.
abstract: PURPOSE: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a surrogate of arterial stiffness that may influence stroke outcomes and potentially affect collateral circulation. We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale (poor, 0-1; good, 2-3). Poor functional outcome was defined as 3-month modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Multivariable logistic and mediation analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ePWV and functional outcomes and to explore direct and indirect pathways. RESULTS: A total of 285 patients were included (mean age, 73.3±11.3 years; 40.4% women). Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with poor collaterals (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.276, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.083-1.503) and poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 1.338, 95% CI 1.121-1.597). In mediation analyses, collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the association between ePWV and poor functional outcome (indirect effect: adjusted β 0.022, 95% CI 0.001-0.053), whereas the direct effect remained significant (adjusted β 0.237, 95% CI 0.115-0.359). Neither the direct effect of ePWV on functional outcome nor the indirect effect through collateral status differed according to BP management strategy. CONCLUSION: Higher ePWV was associated with poor collateral status and unfavorable functional outcome after successful reperfusion. Collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the observed association between ePWV and functional outcome.

title: Early outcomes of the Octapro balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve in an unrestricted cohort of patients with aortic valve stenosis: the MyPro registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on early outcomes of the novel balloon-expandable (BE) Octapro transcatheter heart valve (THV) in real-world practice are limited. We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled. Primary endpoints were VARC-3 technical success, device success, and early safety at 30-day. RESULTS: 2 A total of 303 patients were included (age 78.9 ± 7.4 years; bicuspid 13%). VARC-3 technical success was 97%, peri-procedural mortality 0.3% while no procedural stroke or myocardial infarction were reported. In-hospital guidelines-indicated permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) rate was 13.5%. At discharge mean gradient was 8.4 ± 4.5 mmHg, effective orifice area 1.8 ± 0.3 cm, while moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak was reported in 3.3% of the patients. At 30-day, device success was 92.4% and early safety 80%. All-cause mortality was 2.6%, stroke 0.3%, and guidelines-indicated PPI 14.2%. Mean gradient remained low (9 ± 4 mmHg). Implantation depth and baseline right bundle branch block (RBBB) were independent predictors of PPI. ROC analysis identified an implantation depth threshold of 4.75 mm associated with increased PPI risk. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world registry, the Octapro THV demonstrated high procedural success, favourable early clinical outcomes, and excellent haemodynamic performance. Implantation depth and baseline RBBB were independent predictors of PPI, supporting optimization of implantation technique to mitigate conduction disturbances.

We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled.

title: Transcatheter mitral valve implantation in complex anatomies: Outcomes after prior repair or aborted interventions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with recurrent mitral valve disease after prior repair or persistent disease following an aborted edge-to-edge repair attempt face high risks with conventional surgery. The outcomes of transcatheter mitral valve implantation (TMVI) in these distinct cohorts remain unclear. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included all patients undergoing Tendyne-TMVI between June 2020 and December 2024 for recurrent mitral valve disease after TEER, SMA, balloon valvuloplasty, or persistent mitral valve disease after aborted TEER. Outcomes were assessed using MVARC criteria. RESULTS: Of 85 TMVI procedures, 16 were included (median age 80 years (IQR 70-83); STS 6.9% (IQR 5.6-8.2)). Prior interventions were SMA (37.5%), TEER (12.5%), balloon valvuloplasty (6.2%) and aborted TEER (43.8%). Technical success was 93.8%. At discharge, all patients showed none/trace residual mitral or paravalvular regurgitation, with a mean gradient of 3.9 ± 1.1 mmHg. At 30 days, one patient presented with severe paravalvular regurgitation due to atrialization of the prosthetic valve; no stroke occurred. Acute renal failure requiring dialysis occurred in 18.8%, one major bleeding and rehospitalization for heart failure in 12.5%. Thirty-day mortality was 12.5%. NYHA class improved significantly from 3 to 2 (p = 0.042). MVARC device success at 30 days was 63%. Estimated 1- and 2-year survival was 67% and 56% with 50% of deaths being non-cardiovascular. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected high-risk patients with recurrent or persistent mitral valve disease, Tendyne TMVI achieved durable prosthetic mitral valve function, leading to significant symptomatic improvement. Failure to meet device success was mainly driven by mean mitral gradients exceeding 5 mmHg.

title: Long-term cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome patients with congenital heart disease: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Congenital cardiac anomalies are a major determinant of morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome (TS), yet long-term cardiovascular outcome data remain limited. This study assessed cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, valve dysfunction, and aortic outcomes in TS patients with congenital cardiovascular defects. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 84 TS patients with congenital cardiovascular anomalies were analyzed, with follow-up between 01/1980 and 01/2025. Clinical, demographic, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic variables were reviewed; morbidity and mortality were recorded; descriptive statistics applied. RESULTS: 2 Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) was present in 40 patients (48%) and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) in 29 (35%); 19 patients (23%) had both. At last follow-up (median age 26 years, IQR 31 years), most patients were in NYHA class I (82%) and mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure were 121.7 ± 16.8 mmHg and 76.1 ± 13.1 mmHg, respectively. Sinus rhythm was present in 96% of the patients. In the BAV cohort, aortic regurgitation increased from 6 patients (15%) at first registration to 17 (42.5%) at last follow-up. In the tricuspid aortic valve cohort, aortic regurgitation increased from 1 patient (2.3%) to 12 (27.9%). The last mean ascending aortic diameter indexed to body surface area was 20.4 ± 4.6 mm/m. Aortic dissection occurred in 2 patients (2.7%). Ten patients died during follow-up; median age at death was 41 years (IQR: 52 years), and cardiac causes accounted for at least 50% of mortality. CONCLUSION: BAV and CoA predominated in this TS cohort. Despite generally favorable functional status among survivors, progressive valve dysfunction, aortic complications and cardiovascular mortality support lifelong structured surveillance.

This study assessed cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, valve dysfunction, and aortic outcomes in TS patients with congenital cardiovascular defects. title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of a prediction model for postoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients with periarticular knee fractures.
abstract: The present study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with periarticular knee fractures. A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. Based on ultrasound results, patients were divided into a DVT group (n=83) and a non-DVT group (n=236). Logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors. Subsequently, a nomogram model was established, which was validated via receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The DVT rate was 26.0%. Old age (OR, 1.0228), high American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (OR, 2.2764), greater blood loss (OR, 1.0015), blood transfusion (OR, 2.7917) and high D-dimer levels (OR, 1.0251) were identified as independent risk factors (P<0.05), while living in cities, high hemoglobin, high prealbumin, high Barthel index and high Braden scores served as protective factors (P<0.05). The model yielded an area under the curve value of 0.837. Additionally, the calibration curve showed high accuracy, and DCA validated the favorable clinical applicability of this predictive model. In conclusion, the model performs well in helping doctors to identify high-risk patients and optimize individualized therapeutic strategies.

A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed.

title: Clostridium septicum aortitis and mediastinitis complicating perforated appendicitis in a patient with chronic myelomonocytic leukemia: A case report.
abstract: Clostridium septicum is an aerotolerant anaerobe classically linked to occult colorectal malignancy and hematologic disease, and a rare but frequently fatal cause of nontraumatic infective aortitis; it also causes gas gangrene, osteomyelitis and spondylodiscitis. Survival depends on radical surgical debridement, as antibiotics alone are almost uniformly fatal. We describe a 71-year-old man with untreated chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) who presented with back pain, vomiting and rigors. Computed tomography showed perforated appendicitis with extraluminal air together with mediastinitis and aortitis of the aortic arch and the aorta at the diaphragmatic hiatus. Inflammatory markers were markedly elevated and vasculitis serologies negative. The appendix was managed nonoperatively as he remained hemodynamically stable. Despite broad-spectrum antibiotics, repeat angiography on day 5 showed new aneurysmal dilatation of the arch to 5.1 cm, prompting emergent left carotid-subclavian bypass and thoracic endovascular aortic repair. On day 8, thoracotomy revealed necrotic aortic wall with an exposed endograft, which was debrided and covered with a pedicled latissimus dorsi flap; tissue cultures grew C. septicum. Colonoscopy twelve months earlier had shown only polyps and diverticulosis. He completed six weeks of intravenous ampicillin-sulbactam, was transitioned to lifelong oral suppression for retained prosthetic material, and was discharged on day 57 to long-term acute care, ventilator-dependent. This case shows that C. septicum aortitis may arise from a perforated appendix rather than a colorectal neoplasm, that nonoperative appendicitis management may give inadequate source control in an immunocompromised host, and that survival is attainable with a staged hybrid endovascular-and-open strategy.

Survival depends on radical surgical debridement, as antibiotics alone are almost uniformly fatal. We describe a 71-year-old man with untreated chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) who presented with back pain, vomiting and rigors.

title: [Primary and secondary microsurgical reconstruction in soft tissue sarcomas].
abstract: The reconstruction after soft tissue sarcoma resection is sometimes essential to enable radical R0 resection, limb salvage, satisfactory functional outcomes and timely adjuvant treatment. In a retrospective cohort of 76 soft tissue reconstructions of the lower limbs, predominantly following external resections, wound coverage was consistently performed in a staged manner with a mean interval of 18 days; in more than half of the cases this interval was ≤14 days. A comprehensive review of the scientific literature on soft tissue reconstruction after soft tissue sarcoma resection was conducted. Key prerequisites for maximum oncological safety and reconstructive reliability without delaying adjuvant therapy are plastic and reconstructive expertise within the sarcoma center, expedited pathological margin assessment and close collaboration with vascular surgery and radiotherapy.

title: Antiphospholipid syndrome: epidemiology and outcomes in the evolving criteria era.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a heterogeneous autoimmune thrombo-inflammatory disorder characterized by thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity and an expanding spectrum of microvascular, cardiac, haematological and other systemic manifestations. Although research has provided considerable insights into the pathogenesis and clinical phenotypes of APS, its epidemiology remains difficult to define because estimates depend on case definitions, antibody testing, repeat-testing requirements, testing practices and data sources. Population-based studies suggest that APS is rare, and catastrophic APS is rarer and best understood through registry data. Antiphospholipid antibody positivity alone does not establish APS; transient or low-level positivity can occur without disease, whereas persistent antibodies must be interpreted alongside compatible clinical manifestations. Despite its rarity, APS causes substantial morbidity through recurrent thrombosis, organ damage and adverse pregnancy outcomes, supporting targeted evaluation in unprovoked or recurrent venous thromboembolism, stroke in younger adults and selected pregnancy complications. Apparent differences among populations can reflect ascertainment, access to testing, study design and biological variation. Standardized case definitions, antibody testing and laboratory reporting, together with longitudinal population-based research in ancestry-diverse, paediatric and low-income and middle-income populations, are needed to refine estimates of APS burden and define its clinical spectrum.

title: Complications of Central Venous Catheters in Egyptian Children and Adolescents With Malignancy: A Prospective Single-Center Observational Study.
abstract: Central venous catheters (CVCs) are essential in pediatric oncology but are associated with a considerable risk of complications, particularly in immunocompromised patients. Evidence from low- and middle-income settings remains limited. This prospective observational study was conducted from 2020 to 2023 at a tertiary pediatric oncology center. A total of 141 patients (younger than 18 y), including 382 CVCs, were followed for 5869 catheter-days. Clinical, laboratory, and catheter-related data were collected. Complication rates were expressed per 1000 catheter-days, and risk factors were analyzed using univariate and multivariate models. CVC-related complications occurred in 97/382 devices (25.4%), and mortality was 0.3%. Infectious complications were most frequent (53.1%), followed by vascular (32.8%) and mechanical events (14.1%). Gram-positive organisms predominated in peripheral cultures (26.5%), while Gram-negative pathogens were more common in central cultures (22.4%). Patients with complications had significantly lower leukocyte counts ( P =0.001), neutrophils ( P <0.001), lymphocytes ( P =0.006), and platelets ( P =0.002), with higher D-dimer levels ( P <0.001). Hematological malignancy independently increased complication risk ( P =0.002), while alcohol disinfection of catheter hubs was protective ( P =0.007). Thrombosis represented 85.7% of vascular events and was managed conservatively in most cases. CVC-related complications remain common in pediatric oncology and are influenced by disease-related and modifiable factors. Strengthening infection control practices may significantly reduce complications.
englishSummary: Central venous catheters (CVCs) are essential in pediatric oncology but are associated with a considerable risk of complications, particularly in immunocompromised patients. Evidence from low- and middle-income settings remains limited. This prospective observational study was conducted from 2020 to 2023 at a tertiary pediatric oncology center.

title: Management of Brachial Plexus Neurogenic Tumors: A Retrospective Study of 25 Cases.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: To investigate the clinical characteristics of cervical brachial plexus neurogenic tumors and enhance the diagnostic and therapeutic management of this condition. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 25 patients diagnosed with brachial plexus neurogenic tumors who were treated at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Clinical manifestations, treatment strategies, and follow-up outcomes were systematically summarized. RESULTS: A total of 25 patients were included, treated across multiple departments: otorhinolaryngology-head and neck surgery, neurosurgery, orthopedics, thyroid surgery, and vascular surgery. There were 13 male and 12 female patients, aged 16-76 y, with a disease duration ranging from 1 wk to 2 y, defined as the interval from symptom onset to initial clinical evaluation. The primary presenting symptom was a neck root mass in 21 patients, among whom seven experienced ipsilateral upper limb numbness, soreness, or electric shock-like pain upon palpation and four reported sensory disturbances in the upper extremity or shoulder-back pain. All patients underwent cervical contrast-enhanced computed tomography, and 18 additionally received 3.0 T magnetic resonance imaging. Preoperative ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration cytology was performed in all cases, revealing spindle cell tumors with morphological features suggestive of schwannoma. Of the 25 patients, 23 underwent surgical resection, while two with small tumors (<2 cm), no neurological symptoms, and cytologically benign findings opted for conservative management with close observation. Surgical approaches included the anterior supraclavicular approach, the posterior cervical paravertebral approach, and clavicle-splitting (transclavicular) approach. Postoperative pathological examination confirmed benign schwannoma in 22 cases and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor in one case. Follow-up duration ranged from 12 to 60 mo. Transient postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in five patients, manifesting as limited shoulder abduction, reduced wrist extensor strength, or limb numbness; all deficits resolved within 6 mo following structured rehabilitation programs. CONCLUSIONS: Brachial plexus neurogenic tumors commonly present as a mass in the neck root, with a subset of cases accompanied by neurological symptoms. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are valuable modalities for tumor localization and qualitative characterization. Preoperative fine needle aspiration cytology enables a preliminary assessment of tumor histology. The selection of an appropriate surgical approach should be guided by tumor location and anatomical involvement. Intralesional enucleation is a key strategy for preserving neurological function, and when combined with microsurgical techniques and intraoperative nerve monitoring, even transient postoperative neurological deficits can be effectively managed through structured rehabilitation programs.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 25 patients diagnosed with brachial plexus neurogenic tumors who were treated at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Clinical manifestations, treatment strategies, and follow-up outcomes were systematically summarized.

title: Baricitinib Efficacy Through 4 Years in Responders and Safety up to 5 Years in Adults with Severe Alopecia Areata: Final Results from BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long-term efficacy and safety data are imperative for therapies used to treat severe alopecia areata (AA) because the disease is chronic, loss of response can be devastating to patients, and the safety profile needs to support long-term therapy. Baricitinib, a selective JAK inhibitor, has been approved for severe AA in adults and is being studied in pediatric patients. This study evaluates the final long-term efficacy and safety of baricitinib in adults with severe AA. METHODS: Efficacy was assessed for patients randomized to baricitinib 4 mg or 2 mg who achieved response (Severity of Alopecia Tool [SALT] score ≤ 20) at Week 52 (4 mg, N = 133; 2 mg, N = 72) and stayed on the same dose through Week 200. Proportions of patients maintaining a SALT score ≤ 20 and achieving a Clinician-Reported Outcome Measure for Eyebrow/Eyelash (EB/EL) Hair Loss™ score of 0 or 1 with ≥ 2-point improvement from baseline were reported using the modified last-observation-carried-forward method. Safety is reported as incidence rates (IR) per 100 patient-years at risk for the All BARI AA group (N = 1303) and Extended BARI AA group (N = 948) through 248 weeks of exposure RESULTS: For baricitinib 4 mg and 2 mg, respectively, among Week 52 responders, 115/133 (86.5%) and 61/72 (84.7%) maintained a SALT score ≤ 20 at Week 200. Regrowth of EB/EL hair continued beyond Week 52 and was maintained through Week 200. In up to 5 years of exposure with baricitinib, the IR for serious infections, nonmelanoma skin cancer malignancies, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and major adverse cardiovascular events remained low relative to background rates. No deaths occurred, and adverse event rates remained stable over time. CONCLUSIONS: Within this population, ~ 85% of responders maintained SALT scores ≤ 20 through approximately 4 years with continued benefit for EB/EL. Baricitinib's safety profile remained consistent over 5 years of treatment, in line with prior BRAVE program findings. title: Cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen mapping on admission MRI may predict penumbral tissue fate in acute stroke patients treated successfully with thrombectomy.
abstract: PURPOSE: 2 Infarct growth occurs in most patients despite successful thrombectomy. We evaluated whether a dynamic susceptibility-contrast (DSC) perfusion-MRI surrogate of the cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO) improves prediction of tissue fate within perfusion-diffusion mismatch regions after successful thrombectomy. METHODS: 2 2 In this retrospective analysis of the prospective HIBISCUS-STROKE registry, we included anterior-circulation stroke patients with admission DSC perfusion MRI, recanalization (mTICI ≥ 2b) after thrombectomy, and day-6T2-FLAIR MRI. Admission DSC-derived CMRO, cerebral blood flow (CBF), cerebral blood volume (CBV), and oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) were expressed as ratios to the mirrored contralateral region (rCMRO, rCBF, rCBV, rOEF) within mismatch subregions that infarcted (overlap with the day-6 lesion) or remained viable. All analyses accounted for within-patient clustering (generalized estimating equations, patient-level bootstrap and cross-validation). RESULTS: 2 2 2 Of 321 screened patients, 134 were included (median age, 71 years; 57.5 % men; median NIHSS score, 15), yielding 245 mismatch subregions (111 infarcted, 134 viable). rCMRO, rCBF, and rCBV were lower in infarcted than in viable subregions, whereas rOEF did not differ. rCMROprovided the best discrimination of infarction (AUC, 0.77; 95 % CI, 0.72-0.82), higher than rCBF (0.74; P = 0.04), rCBV (0.73; P = 0.001), and rOEF (0.52; P < 0.001); the gain over rCBF was modest (integrated discrimination improvement, 0.064; 95 % CI, 0.026-0.110). rCMRO<0.66 was selected in all cross-validation folds and independently predicted infarction (adjusted odds ratio, 8.02; 95 % CI, 4.60-14.01). CONCLUSIONS: 2 A DSC-MRI surrogate of CMROon admission discriminated infarct-destined from viable tissue within the perfusion-diffusion mismatch after successful thrombectomy, with a modest but consistent advantage over conventional perfusion metrics.

title: Deep Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest Duration and Neurologic Outcomes in Pulmonary Thromboendarterectomy.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) is essential for pulmonary thromboendarterectomy (PTE). The optimal safe duration of DHCA remains controversial. This study evaluates the association between total DHCA duration and postoperative neurologic events and major adverse cardiac events (MACEs) following PTE. METHODS: All PTE patients at a single institution from October 2017 to March 2025 were retrospectively analyzed and categorized into "standard" and "extended" cohorts. Extended DHCA was defined as total time >1 standard deviation above the median (60 min). DHCA was performed at 20°C and limited to 20-min intervals with 10 min of reperfusion. Outcomes assessed included 30-d neurologic events and MACE. Independent associations were evaluated using inverse probability weighting with Firth bias reduction methods. RESULTS: Extended DHCA patients exhibited higher residual pulmonary vascular resistance (4.0 versus 3.0 Wood Units, P = 0.032) but both groups were equally likely to achieve a 50% reduction from baseline (extended 44.8% versus standard 62%, P = 0.097). On inverse probability weighting analysis, DHCA duration was not independently associated with neurologic events (odds ratio [OR] 0.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.01-8.04, P = 0.877). Peripheral arterial disease was independently associated with neurologic events (OR 22.3, 95% CI 7.46-4730, P < 0.001) along with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation use (preoperative and intraoperative) (OR 82.7). Extended DHCA time was independently associated with MACE (OR 6.46, 95% CI 0.90-228, P = 0.010), along with preoperative pulmonary vascular resistance (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.00-1.84, P = 0.027). CONCLUSIONS: Extended DHCA was not independently associated with neurological events after PTE but was independently associated with MACE. Balancing total circulatory arrest duration with complete bilateral endarterectomy is paramount for successful PTE surgery.

title: Beyond the Threshold: Continuous Creatinine Change and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) worsens outcomes in acute ischemic stroke, but threshold-based definitions do not capture prognostic information from subthreshold changes. We tested whether early creatinine change within 48 hours of EVT conveys graded prognostic information beyond dichotomous CA-AKI. METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of the CAN-REST registry (Contrast-Associated Nephropathy After Endovascular Stroke Treatment), a retrospective multicenter observational cohort study of 6638 EVT-treated adults with acute ischemic stroke enrolled at 73 centers in 16 countries between January 1 and December 31, 2023. Early creatinine change was quantified as the natural logarithm ratio of 48-hour creatinine to baseline creatinine (ln[48-hour/baseline creatinine]), with CA-AKI defined per Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria (≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5× baseline rise within 48 hours). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified baseline and periprocedural covariates examined associations with 90-day modified Rankin Scale shift and in-hospital mortality; linear versus restricted cubic spline specification was selected by likelihood ratio testing, and contrasts were estimated at ±10%, ±25%, and ±50%. RESULTS: Greater creatinine worsening within 48 hours of EVT was independently associated with an unfavorable 90-day modified Rankin Scale shift (adjusted common odds ratio per 1-unit log-ratio increase, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.07-2.04]; linear) and in-hospital mortality (nonlinear dose-response, of larger magnitude). A 10% increase in creatinine at 48 hours-well below Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes threshold-was associated with worse functional outcome (adjusted common odds ratio, 1.04 [95% CI, 1.01-1.07]) and death (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.13-1.32]); a 10% decrease in creatinine at 48 hours was associated with lower odds of both outcomes (adjusted common odds ratio, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.93-0.99]; adjusted odds ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.65-0.86]). The functional-outcome association concentrated at upper modified Rankin Scale cut-points (severe disability, death); effect modification by baseline renal function was not significant. CONCLUSIONS: Early creatinine change after EVT conveys graded, outcome-specific prognostic information extending below formal CA-AKI thresholds, with a dose-response detectable at changes as modest as ±10%, complementing binary CA-AKI as a framework for post-EVT renal risk assessment. title: Comparison of recommendations for initial adult traumatic brain injury management across clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements: a scoping review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. We conducted a scoping review to identify, map, and compare recommendations for the initial medical management of adult TBI. METHODS: Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, guideline repositories, and gray literature for English or Spanish language documents published from 2010 to 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, charted recommendations across domains, and rated agreement using a priori categories; discrepancies were resolved by consensus or third reviewer. RESULTS: Sixteen documents met inclusion criteria, including guidelines, consensus statements, and best-practice recommendations. Broad agreement existed for early neurological assessment, airway protection, avoidance of hypotension and hypoxemia, and timely neuroimaging. Heterogeneity remained in blood pressure and cerebral perfusion pressure targets, repeat imaging, definitions of neurological deterioration, escalation criteria, observation protocols, and discharge processes. Anticonvulsant prophylaxis and venous thromboembolism prevention were inconsistently addressed. Blood-based biomarkers appeared in only three documents and were limited to computed tomography decision-making. CONCLUSIONS: Although the fundamental principles of care were largely consistent, important differences remain in their operational implementation. Greater harmonization of clinical definitions and management pathways may facilitate more consistent application of evidence-based recommendations across healthcare settings.

title: Association between admission D-dimer levels and post-stroke epilepsy risk: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) is a severe complication following acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet early identification of patients at high risk remains challenging. This study evaluated the association between baseline D-dimer levels and incident PSE within one year after AIS. METHODS: 2 In this secondary analysis of a multicenter retrospective cohort, 21,459 patients with first-ever AIS were included. D-dimer was modeled as a log-transformed continuous variable. Multivariable logistic regression with progressive adjustment, restricted cubic spline analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: The median baseline D-dimer level was 0.92 mg/L (IQR 0.65-1.49). PSE occurred in 936 patients (4.36%). After full adjustment, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with a 3.3-fold increase in PSE odds (OR 3.33, 95% CI 2.94-3.78). The association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with deep vein thrombosis (OR 3.86, 95% CI 3.37-4.43), atrial fibrillation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 3.04-4.04), or extreme D-dimer values (OR 3.41, 95% CI 2.99-3.91). A non-linear relationship was observed, with PSE risk rising more steeply at higher D-dimer levels. The C-statistic for the fully adjusted model was 0.968. CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline D-dimer levels were independently associated with an increased risk of PSE within one year after AIS. As a routinely available biomarker, D-dimer may inform risk assessment in acute stroke units; however, external validation in independent cohorts with prospective PSE ascertainment is required before clinical implementation.

title: Deterioration of Peri-Infarct Microvascular Hemodynamics Following Successful Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Predicts Infarct Growth.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion. METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study from the University of California, Los Angeles, patients with acute ischemic stroke from 2015 to 2020 were included if they had excellent reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2c) and diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MRIs at baseline, immediately PT, and 24 to 48 hours after thrombectomy. Peri-infarct regions were defined as time to maximum ≥6-second regions on baseline MRI that were not infarcted on immediate PT MRI. Following image coregistration, quantitative values of perfusion parameters, including RTH, were obtained from peri-infarct regions on immediate PT MRI. Two primary outcomes were assessed: (1) infarct growth ≥10 mL and (2) poor functional outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale score >2). Associations between clinical and imaging parameters and outcomes were evaluated using univariate analysis. Age, sex, and covariates that were significant in univariate analysis were included in logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: P P P P Among 47 patients included in the analysis (62% women; mean age, 72±13 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 14), 20 (43%) patients had substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcome. Peri-infarct RTH was significantly (=0.005) higher in patients with infarct growth >10 mL than those without and remained as an independent predictor (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-2.0];=0.04). Similarly, the peri-infarct RTH was significantly higher (<0.001) in patients with poor functional outcomes than those with good functional outcomes and remained as a significant predictor of poor functional outcome (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-1.9];=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Increased peri-infarct RTH on immediate PT MRI predicts substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcomes in successfully reperfused patients with acute ischemic stroke. Results highlight the role of microvascular dysfunction depicted by elevated RTH as a potential marker of no-reflow phenomenon despite excellent macrovascular reperfusion.

title: What Preclinical Medical Students Value When Choosing a Surgical Career: A Cluster Analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Understanding what students value when choosing a surgical career and whether early exposure changes them is crucial for effective recruitment. This study used a prospective preclinical surgical skills course to evaluate specialty choice factors and determine whether improved skills influence them or interest in the sponsoring specialty. METHODS: Forty-seven preclinical medical students enrolled in an 8-wk vascular surgery-sponsored elective skills course. Students completed standardized precourse and postcourse surveys assessing interest in surgery and the sponsoring specialty, confidence in surgical abilities, perceptions of surgery, and eleven specialty choice factors. K-means cluster analysis identified groups of factors by importance. Surgical performance was assessed using knot tying and suturing metrics. Normally distributed variables were compared using paired t-tests; non-normal and Likert scale variables using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: Students significantly improved across all skills metrics. Median attending-rated competency scores improved from 1 to 4/5 for knot tying and suturing (both P < 0.001). Interest in the sponsoring specialty did not change and remained lower than interest in surgery overall (P < 0.01). K-means clustering identified a high-importance cluster comprising personality fit, early specialty exposure, attending lifestyle, mentorship, attending workload, and income potential, and a low-importance cluster comprising residency-related factors including training length, research years, competitiveness, resident lifestyle, and resident workload. The only factor that changed postcourse was early exposure (P = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: Preclinical students prioritize attending-level factors and early exposure over residency-related factors when choosing a specialty. Despite significant skill improvement, interest in the sponsoring specialty did not increase. Recruitment efforts should prioritize mentorship, early exposure, and attending lifestyle-not skills training alone.

title: Hybrid management of primary aortic mural thrombus with mesenteric embolization.
abstract: Primary aortic mural thrombus with visceral embolization is a rare and life-threatening condition without an established treatment strategy. We report the case of a 40-year-old woman with thoracoabdominal primary aortic mural thrombus and embolization to the superior mesenteric and common hepatic arteries. She was treated using a hybrid approach consisting of large-bore aspiration thrombectomy with the Symphony Thrombectomy System (Imperative Care, Inc), temporary aortic flow control using a trilobed occlusion balloon, intravascular ultrasound-guided thoracic endovascular aortic repair, and selective conversion to open superior mesenteric artery thrombectomy with patch angioplasty. The patient recovered without bowel resection or distal embolic complications, demonstrating the feasibility of this staged hybrid strategy.

title: Perioperative outcomes after thoracic aortic surgery in Johannesburg: a retrospective observational cohort study, 1995-2023.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thoracic aortic diseases require complex surgery, and outcomes data from African populations are scarce. We described the patient characteristic profile, documented risk factors, and perioperative outcomes of patients undergoing thoracic aortic surgery at a quaternary hospital in South Africa. METHODS: In a retrospective cohort study reported per the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines, we included patients aged 18 yr or older who underwent open thoracic aortic surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital between 1995 and 2023. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. We assessed correlates using modified Poisson regression with robust variance (risk ratios [RRs]). RESULTS: P vs Of 366 patients (median age 48 yr [inter-quartile range 37-59]; 219 [59.8%] male), diagnoses were dissection in 157 (42.9%), aneurysm in 157 (42.9%), traumatic rupture in 26 (7.1%), and other in 26 (7.1%). In-hospital mortality was 21.9% (80 of 366; 95% confidence interval [CI] 17.7-26.4) and did not differ significantly across diagnosis groups (=0.693), being identical after dissection and aneurysm (22.9% in each). Prolonged operative duration (>600 min) was the only variable independently associated with mortality (adjusted RR 7.2; 95% CI 1.5-34.9), an imprecise, sparse-data estimate. Mortality was numerically higher in female than male patients (26.2%19.2%) but this difference was not significant after adjustment (adjusted RR 1.30; 95% CI 0.89-1.89); age and diagnosis were not independently associated. CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality after thoracic aortic surgery was 21.9%. Prolonged operative duration was associated with in-hospital mortality, although the estimate was imprecise, and operative duration is likely to be a marker of procedural complexity and adverse intraoperative course rather than an independently modifiable risk factor. The findings support intensive postoperative care.
